canonical_claim: The Stage B strategic review's concentration proposal, in dependency order: (1) a `FencedCatalogWriter` primitive constructed once per mount from `(admitted_generation, check_fence_or_throw)` that owns `casUpdate`/`casAdmitEntry`/`publishCkpt` dispatch and re-checks the fence inside every CAS attempt, replacing the two threaded fence parameters at every call site; (2) collapse namespace-life resolution to three named entry points — `lifeIfCataloged` (read), `resolveNamespaceLife` (the sole writer-mint path after the R12 fix), `liveUniverse` (GC/fsck/sweep/decommission) — retiring `resolveLifeOrSentinel`; (3) make removal ordering (prune GC-held state before entry delete) the load-bearing invariant so incarnation-scoped cursor re-keying and half the coexistence tests become unnecessary.

The standalone `tree` `ObjectKind` was excised on 2026-07-03; `ObjectKind` is now Blob-only, and `toEventKind` only handles `Blob`.; The single-value `ObjectKind` enum was deliberately retained and was not removed despite spec item D1f because it is threaded through about 100 consumers, including the parameter/field types of `observeAndAdmit`, `uploadFromSource`, `decodeEnvelopeHeader`, `magicFor`, `retiredLogicalSize`, `EnvelopeHeader::kind`, `RetiredEntry::kind`, the `CasGcOutcomes` codec, and `Fsck/GcObserved`; removing it would be a refactor rather than clean subtraction.

Lesson recorded from the deposed-leader stray-Clean investigation: a formal model that is safer than the code hides real bugs. The original `CaRetiredInRun` TLA gate did not model the deposed leader and stayed green; a first attempted fix made the model advisory-add-only and also went green, but this was a false-green that masked the code's actual behavior (`clearSparedMeta` really does clear-to-Clean pre-CAS) until the BLOCKED verdict and a not-weaken-invariants discipline caught the discrepancy.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's top identified risk (R1) is that an extraction changes lock discipline: the publish lane's correctness depends on the two-phase carve happening under one continuous lock hold and the install region not allocating; the mitigation is to extract only pure functions called from the same place under the same lock (so discipline is unchanged by construction) and to gate on a soak run, not just gtests.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's R2 risk is `Pool` facade churn, since B6 touches the class everything depends on; the mitigation is to do that extraction last and keep `Pool` as a delegating facade so call sites are untouched.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's R3 risk is that `docs/superpowers/cas/11-walkthrough.md` cites roughly 200 file:line references that workstream B invalidates; the mitigation is to refresh the walkthrough as the final step of workstream B, before carving, since it is the document reviewers read first.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's R4 risk is that workstream A3 may be reshaped in upstream review after it has already landed in the fork; the mitigation is to keep A3's fork commits identical to what is proposed upstream and treat upstream feedback as a follow-up to both.

A codex review of the publish-confirm/ref-lane-safety landing raised three footprint objections against the upstream-coupling-minimization rule; two were knowingly accepted as tradeoffs and recorded as accepted (not debt) rather than corrected: `DataPartsExchange.h` exposing `allow_ca_relink` and CAS-specific service helpers beyond the opaque enum, and the confirm/relink logic spanning more functions per side than the rule's ideal shape.

The publish-confirm/ref-lane-safety design deliberately uses two distinct types for the same confirm answer across the exchange boundary — `ConfirmAnswer` in the ledger and `CasConfirmAnswer` in the exchange wire header, and `PreparedPartWrite` (CAS-internal) exposed through the abstract `ICaPreparedRelink` — so that `DataPartsExchange.cpp` needs no CAS-internal headers, keeping the one type mapping confined to a single implementation file.

The branch-reconstruction carve script accepts, as a residual risk, that a file moved between source areas (e.g. a gtest moved into a layer directory) silently changes which commit carries it; this is accepted because the commit grouping is presentational only.
The ref-table snapshot-log Phase 1 plan has zero deliberate deviations from its spec; Phase 2 items are excluded per the plan's Global Constraints, not silently dropped.
Codex triage finding №18 was not given its own task because the root fix in Task 2 collapses it; the affected list-branch change is called out explicitly inside Task 2 rather than as a separate item.

The relink/seam TLA+ model deliberately introduces three controls the spec does not name (_ctl_v11nomarker, _ctl_distinctns, _ctl_skipidentity) because a flip with no control would be a coincidence and a green with no scoping statement would be a silent gap; it also models the full wedge lifecycle (hazards and happy path) beyond what section 12 of the spec asks for, because three drafts proved that modelling rule 3 without the wedge lifecycle produced sabotages that were red for unreachable states and greens resting on missing ones.

The standalone Merkle `treeId` design and `CasTreeCodec` are not implemented in the current code because the rev.15 `PartManifest` redesign replaced the standalone Tree object.; The separate intermediate/Merkle `treeId` tree-layer design—content-addressed `trees/<T>` objects forming a Merkle DAG of immutable folders, with tree hashes carrying `child_gen` inside the tree identity—was rejected because it added key-space and GC edge complexity without benefit beyond recursive subtrees and identity decoupling; `child_gen` inside tree identity forced ancestor rebuilds whenever a blob's generation floor moved, the 404->LIST degraded read path for generation resolution added latency and complexity, and the generation-in-key model required durable per-hash floors, epochs, per-build pins, quiescence machinery, and Keeper as a required component. Tree objects are manifest-internal, and the `trees/` key prefix and `ObjectKind::Tree` were removed entirely on 2026-07-03, leaving only `Blob` in `ObjectKind`.

The original EBR/epoch GC model `CaGcCore.tla` was removed as superseded by the incarnation-token design.; The original epoch-based reclamation GC with a global epoch and per-writer pins was superseded by the incarnation-token design because no epoch machinery exists in the shipped code.

The raw-body and terminal-tombstone variants were rejected because removing the in-body incarnation tag makes the body etag content-derived and prevents exact-token deletion from missing a resurrected body.; The raw-body v1 cut was rejected because dropping the in-body incarnation tag fixed the body etag to content and removed the protection that makes exact-token deletion miss a resurrected body.

Per-incarnation blob keys were rejected because they require a 404-to-LIST generation-resolution path, propagate incarnation into manifests, and need additional floors or pins.; Per-incarnation blob/body keys such as `blobs/xx/<hash>.<incarnation>` were rejected because they require generation resolution by `LIST` and a `404 → LIST` or `404-then-LIST` read path, recreate the generation-in-key race, propagate or leak incarnation into manifests and parents, and break pure-content manifests and the pure-content/FUSE-ready design.

The rev.6 proposal was superseded by the approved rev.6 design because sealing at the greatest listed transaction ID was insufficient.; The proposal's recovery-seal-at-listed-maximum rule was later corrected to the dead-epoch upper-bound rule because an unresolved predecessor ID can exceed the greatest listed ID.

The fetch-handoff retention-pin design was superseded on 2026-07-23 by a publish-confirm design in which the receiver confirms the sender's committed ref before promoting; the superseding design removes the pool-global pin and GC changes.; The retention-pin design was rejected because it would add a pool-global GC overlay, union folding, removal deferral, and owner-liveness machinery to the most safety-critical component.

Stock `RESTORE` generates a fresh coordinated UUID, so it is not an exact-`RootNamespace` reuse route; shadow-name reuse and explicit-UUID replay remain supported reuse routes.; Permanent exact-`RootNamespace` non-reuse would avoid generation-based aliasing only by refusing supported exact-name reuse workflows, including shadow names and explicit UUID replay.

topic: full-scale P0 campaign found six O(N) cost families
canonical_claim: The full-scale P0 campaign found six O(N) cost families: GC round O(pool objects), scratch equal to full part size, replicated `OPTIMIZE` double-spill, wide-part O(columns), partitioned INSERT O(partitions), and startup O(refs).
The rev.5 five-second grace floor was measured to cause approximately 20–26 GB/hour of ref snapshot traffic per node in the cited soak.

In the measured 500-partition profile, `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::finishDelayed` commits partitions serially, the ref-ledger batch size is 1.0, and `CasRefBatchFlushes` equals `CasRefBatchedMutations` at 1026.
